name: Faroe Islands
tagline: Sheer cliffs, grass-roofed villages and sea-level waterfalls
summary: The Faroe Islands are 18 rugged islands in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Norway. Photograph the Múlafossur waterfall dropping into the sea at Gásadalur, hike to the lake that hangs above the ocean at Sørvágsvatn, take the ferry to Mykines for puffins, and stay in Tórshavn, one of the world's smallest capitals.
seasonNote: May to August for long days and puffins (Mykines, roughly May to August); weather changes fast all year.
arrival: Flights from Copenhagen take 2 hours; Vágar Airport is 45 minutes from Tórshavn by tunnel.
gettingAround: Rent a car; undersea tunnels link the main islands (some tolled), ferries and helicopters reach the rest.
cashTip: The Faroese króna is on a par with the Danish krone, and cards work everywhere. Tipping is not expected.
foodTip: Fermented ræst lamb and fish, fresh langoustines and Faroese salmon.
